title: Check yourself: sealed types beside enums and packages

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: The page compares sealed classes with enums. Which of these can a sealed hierarchy do that an enum cannot?

options.text: Limit its possible kinds to a fixed set declared in one place
options.says: The page says both sealed classes and enums represent a fixed set of possibilities, so this is no difference.

options.text: Create many instances of each subtype, each holding its own state
options.says: The page's answer on enums: enum constants are singleton instances, while a sealed class can have many instances of each subclass, each with its own state.

options.text: Give each of its kinds exactly one shared instance at runtime
options.says: That describes an enum: the page says enum constants are singleton instances.

questions.stem: A sealed class sits in the unnamed module. Where must its permitted subclasses be declared, by the page's rules?

options.text: Within the one package that also holds it
options.says: The page's rules: in the same module, or in the same package when the sealed class is in the unnamed module.

options.text: In any package found on the same classpath
options.says: The page asks for the same package when the sealed class is in the unnamed module, not merely the same classpath.

options.text: In any named module that can read it
options.says: The page requires the same module as the sealed class, and the same package when that module is unnamed.

concepts: Permitted subclasses live in the sealed class's module, or in its package when it is in the unnamed module.
Unlike enum constants, which are singletons, a sealed hierarchy can have many instances of each subtype with their own state.
